title: Inference Kitchen Notebook — cache & batch recipes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for papers/blogs and conference takeaways that feel like recipes I want to try on Redwood serving runtime. Tone = kitchen notes: short, actionable, messy.

Quick hits (reads + one-line take):
- "Attention as cache" (blog, May 2026): strong intuition for using attention patterns as a lightweight cache — cheap indexing by attention keys rather than storing full KV blobs. Worth testing for short-session chat where state overlaps a lot.
- arXiv:2406.12345 — 'Sparse-KV for Long Conversations' (skim): shows >2x throughput with chunked sparse retrieval into KV layers, avoids full-sequence attention for old context. Promising for low-cost long-chat mode if combined with prefetched prefix caches.
- MLSys 2026 talk: 'Batching heuristics for heterogeneous latency SLOs' — empirically shows latency-tail wins by mixing short-deadline routing and opportunistic batching windows. Concrete rule: allow 3–7ms extra wait for high-probability short batches, drop to immediate routing after 10ms.

Paper recipe ideas (what I'll try):
1) Prefix-as-embedding cache (cheap, staged eviction)
   - Ingredient: small embedding index for recent N turns (N=16) + cosine lookup for prompt prefix match threshold 0.78
   - Prep: compute prefix embeddings client-side when request arrives; if match, attach compressed prefix tokens (quantized int8) to request; runtime skips recomputing kv for matched prefix segment
   - Metrics: token-savings, end-to-end latency delta, accuracy on hallucination probe set (prompt set A)

2) Opportunistic micro-batching for tail-slo routes
   - Ingredient: per-route short-window buffer (max wait 5ms), fallback threshold when queue length>8 or route SLO breach predicted
   - Prep: use routing policy with priorities (gold/silver/free) and per-request deadline header; in simulated load, tune wait threshold to trade-off P95 vs throughput
   - Metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency, throughput, batch size distribution, model cost per 1M tokens

3) Quantize-First Cache: store cached KV in low-bit (4-bit) layout and expand lazily on GPU if recompute needed
   - Idea: saves memory bandwidth for cold-cache reads; needs microbench for decompression cost vs memory fetch cost

Notes from MLSys session (hand-scribbles):
- Rule of thumb from demo: small, frequent batches beat large rare batches for CPU-side overhead reasons when sequence length < 512.
- Warm-up penalty for quantized kernels was visible for first 50 steps — include warmup traffic in preview windows.

Experiment details (practical steps):
- Create synthetic workload generator with three modes: short-consult (len 50, high repetition), long-narrative (len 800, low repetition), mixed-burst (poisson arrivals + bursts)
- Hook generator to dedicated cluster staging (small pool of 4 A100 equiv GPUs) and to local sim harness to iterate quickly
- Instrument: per-token cost, kv-cache hit ratio, kernel occupancy, PCIe read size, latency percentiles, memory used per model shard
- Baselines: current production config (no prefix embedding cache, 0ms wait micro-batching)

Prompts / probes to evaluate quality regressions:
- Probe set A: 120 customer-like conversations that depend on long-span coreference; check for pronoun resolution after prefix elision
- Probe set B: hallucination-sensitivity set — questions that surface if a model drops evidence because of aggressive cache compression
- Metric: semantic-ROUGE (embedding based similarity) + binary hallucination flag from lightweight classifier

Unresolved questions / risks: 
- How much client CPU burden is acceptable for computing prefix embeddings? Will customers object? Could move to gateway-side service.
- Risk: cache-matching false positives leading to context bleed across sessions; need strict session keys + conservative thresholds.
- Interaction with rollouts: when a model variant changes attention geometry (e.g., new layernorm scale), cached embeddings/kv mismatches could cause stale hits — need model-versioned cache keys.

Immediate next actions (week):
- Draft GH experiment PR: 'inference/kitchen/prefix-cache-sim' — create sim harness + small metric dashboard (Devon) — target by 2026-06-09
- Quick microbenchmark: quantize-first cache read latency on one dev machine (Mira) — target by 2026-06-04
- Slack ping #inference-kitchen for volunteers to run probe set A on their dedicated dev models

Random sparks (brainstorm):
- "Breadcrumbs" design: store tiny hash of prior tokens (64-bit) and a compressed summary (16B) to cheaply detect repetition without heavy lookup
- Cooperative client-server warming: client sends small 'digest' of recent convo during idle frames (on mobile) to prewarm KV on next request

References & bookmarks (quick links I kept):
- Sparse-KV paper: arXiv:2406.12345
- MLSys 'Batching heuristics' session notes (video link copied to GH issue)
- Blog: 'attention-cache patterns' (internal link)
raw_text_preview: Kitchen-style notes: recipes to try for prefix caching, opportunistic batching, and quantized caches. Includes experiment plan, probes, open questions, and small to-dos.
